key_insight: The paper shows that compiler figure-of-merit quality can be improved by learning from both circuit structure and hardware context, with weighted PST (wPST) providing a more informative target than standard gate-count or depth metrics.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum compiler designers a practical way to rank hardware-compatible circuits more accurately, improving execution success prediction without the cost of full circuit simulation or trial execution.
method: Defined an ideal FoM and proposed wPST, which weights success probabilities across individual qubits rather than only the full state.
Built machine-learning models that combine quantum circuit features with device hardware data to predict PST and wPST quickly.
Added a two-step method for non-transpiled circuits: predict extra gates first, then estimate wPST while accounting for device coherence times.
evidence_signal: In numerical simulations and experiments on quantum processors, the learned FoMs improved correlation with true PST/wPST by more than 50% compared with commonly used metrics.
watch_item: The two-step prediction pipeline depends on accurate gate-addition and hardware-coherence estimates, so performance may degrade when device conditions drift or compilation patterns differ from training data.
paper_title: Comparing and learning figures of merit for quantum circuit compilation
